hypothesis: Jerome's question 'how long does it stay good?' when the data are not first-order Markov (2 Nov 2026; the user approved the design and these predictions). The truth is an AR(2) with Laplace innovations at E03's lag-one correlation 0.85 and variance 1, so a first-order method sees the same lag-one covariance at every phi2 and only the memory beyond one step changes. Three questions: (1) is first-order EM-BP's loss structural (a floor that data do not lower)? (2) where does it stop beating the networks? (3) does enlarging the state to the pair (a_{t-1}, a_t), which makes the chain first order again, restore the advantage? The misspecification is measured by delta, the KL rate to the best first-order chain: for a Gaussian process -1/2 sum_{j >= 2} log(1 - pi_j^2) over the partial autocorrelations (for the AR(2) -(L-2)/(2L) log(1 - phi2^2)); for the Laplace AR(2) exactly (L-2)/L I(a_t; a_{t-2} | a_{t-1}). The same delta places a real series on the axis: the Horns Rev wind of E59 has a lag-2 partial autocorrelation of -0.2884 and small ones after it (|pi_j| <= 0.035 for j = 3-6; delta_gauss over lags 2-24 0.04451), as far from first order as phi2 = +-0.3. E08 measured the Gaussian AR(2) with a first-order kernel against the window CNN at M = 512, 2048; E62 adds Laplace innovations, the pair-state repair, small M, delta, and wind.
design: CHAINS: a_t = phi1 a_{t-1} + phi2 a_{t-2} + eps, eps Laplace with Var (1 - 0.85^2)(1 - phi2^2), phi1 = 0.85 (1 - phi2), phi2 in (-0.3, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6), started from the stationary law (600 burn-in steps from 0). L = 32, E03's twelve levels, M in (128, 512, 2048), seeds 0-7, 1024 validation and 2048 test chains per (phi2, seed), E62's tags. REFERENCE: pair-state BP (markov_score.pair_bp) with the true K2 and its stationary pair law on 151 points over [-8, 8] (relative score difference to 201 points: below 7.5e-4 in the calibration). ARMS: first (the thesis mixture, C = 8, by EM through first-order grid BP on 401 points from one noisy view per chain, the kernel's own invariant law as initial law; E56's selection on the validation risk, E33's ladder to 1200); pair (a two-lag mixture-innovation kernel a_t = phi1 a_{t-1} + phi2 a_{t-2} + eps, eps a C = 8 Gaussian mixture, 2 + 3C parameters, by EM through pair-state BP on 101 points, its own stationary pair law as initial law; ladder (10, 20, 40, 80, 120, 160, 220, 300); same selection); mlp and window (E03's screened winners on the clean chains); lmmse (the LMMSE of the true AR(2) covariance). WIND (P5): E59's transformed Horns Rev series and splits; training windows of L = 32 from the training years (N in (32, 128, 512, 1917), E59's windows), test windows from the test year; kernels by clean-data maximum likelihood: first (the C = 8 mixture, first order) and pair (the two-lag mixture); the networks as above. No exact reference exists on real data, so the wind metric is the pooled denoising error against the clean value, sum (alpha/delta)^2 |m_hat - a|^2 over sites and levels: it equals the score error plus a term that is the same for every method, so it ranks methods exactly as the score error does (paired comparisons only).

predeclared_predictions.P1: Structural bias: at M = 2048 the seed-mean of first is within +-25% of the calibrated first-order floor (first_order_floor below) at every phi2 >= 0.2, and its seed-mean at 2048 is not more than 10% below its seed-mean at 512 at those phi2.
predeclared_predictions.P2: The repair: pair below first at M = 2048 in >= 7/8 seeds at every phi2 >= 0.1.
predeclared_predictions.P3: The break-even: at M = 2048 the seed-mean of first is below the best network's (the lower seed-mean of mlp and window) at phi2 <= 0.1 (phi2 in 0, 0.1) and above it at phi2 >= 0.4 (0.4, 0.6).
predeclared_predictions.P4: The repair restores the advantage: pair below the best network at every phi2 and every M in >= 7/8 seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P5: Wind: pair's wind denoising error below first's in >= 7/8 seeds (training subsets) at every N.

descriptive.D1: Seed-mean risk per phi2 x arm x M, against delta_gauss and delta_exact (the robustness figure), with the calibrated first-order floor and the linear floor drawn in.
descriptive.D2: The break-even delta, interpolated between the phi2 values.
descriptive.D3: The fitted (phi1, phi2) of pair against the truth; wall time per fit of first and pair.
descriptive.D4: Wind: every arm's wind denoising error by N; wind's delta on the D1 axis.
descriptive.D5: Appendix (AR(p) cost): pair-state BP time per chain for p = 1, 2, 3 at n = 51, 101 (p = 3 on the triple state, laptop) and one coarse-grid (n = 51) Laplace AR(3) reference against its first-order projection.
